name: Bronze Vowels
description: Struck bells that open their mouths as they fade: what each bell keeps ringing spells a slow vowel, and the last one struck teaches the others its word.

params.name: Metal
params.description: What is struck: a tuned body, a wooden bar, a gong plate, a cast bell or a glass. It sets the overtones and how they die. Taken up by the next strike.

params.name: Stray
params.description: How far the overtones stand from the harmonics of the key. Turned down, the metal is tuned like a voice; turned up, it is raw. The note and its hum stay in tune.

params.name: Mallet
params.description: What wakes the bell: a soft felt head, a wooden stick that stands out and drops, a fingernail that thins the low end, or a breath. Taken up by the next strike.

params.name: Hardness
params.description: How hard the mallet is. A hard one wakes more of the high overtones and speaks sooner, a soft one leaves the low ones alone.

params.name: Strike point
params.description: Where on the metal the strike falls, from the rim to the waist. It takes out some overtones and brings up others, and the vowel is drawn with what is left.

params.name: Knock
params.description: The sound of the mallet itself at the strike: a thump, a knock, a tick or a puff of air.

params.name: Swell
params.description: How slowly the bell comes up. Short is a strike, long is a swell that already has its vowel as it arrives.

params.name: Word
params.description: The word each bell says while it rings. It is said to its end, then back to its beginning, for as long as there is something to say it with.

params.name: Speaking time
params.description: How long the word takes, once through. Above the note C5 a word is heard as bright and dark instead of as vowels.

params.name: Clarity
params.description: How much the overtones outside the vowel are damped. At the bottom the bell does not speak; at the top only what spells the vowel is left ringing.

params.name: Tract
params.description: The size of the mouth. Down is a giant with low, dark vowels, up is a child with high, bright ones. The pitch of the note stays.

params.name: Contagion
params.description: How the ringing bells answer the last one struck. Up, they come round to its vowel, down, to the opposite one. Either way it rings the held ones awake again.

params.name: Own pace
params.description: How much the keys differ in speaking. Turned up, low bells speak slowly and late and high ones quickly, so a chord says its word in turns.

params.name: Ring
params.description: How long the note of the bell rings. Overtones ring for less, by the metal and by Wear.

params.name: Wear
params.description: How much sooner the high overtones die than the low ones. A worn bell goes dark and round as it rings, a new one keeps its brightness.

params.name: Hum
params.description: The tone an octave under the note, as a large bell has it.

params.name: Beat
params.description: How far apart the two halves of each low overtone stand. Their beating makes the bell turn slowly, then shake. Low bells turn more slowly.

params.name: Sing
params.description: How much a held key feeds its bell. At the bottom it dies by itself; at the top it sings the word for as long as the key is down.

params.name: Air
params.description: Breath in the bell while it rings: a whisper through the same mouth, and overtones that flutter with it.

params.name: Damp on release
params.description: What letting the key go does. At the bottom the bell rings on and a swell comes up to its end, at the top a hand stops it at once.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far the overtones and the halves of each pair are spread between the speakers.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Overall output level of the instrument.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Each partial is a turning unit vector whose level is worked out on a control clock; the vowel is a moving rule for how fast each partial falls and how far. Formant places are textbook averages; levels, ring times and the metals' ratios are voiced by measurement, not taken from particular instruments.
